facts.fact: Algeria's High Commission for Digitalisation says the experimental data exchange over the sovereign network (IRIES) succeeded and real data exchange has begun between 33 ministerial sectors and public bodies connected by fibre outside the internet.
The High Commission for Digitalisation says 33 ministerial sectors and public bodies now exchange data in practice over the sovereign network.

The High Commission for Digitalisation says it is preparing the launch of a national interoperability platform to exchange data between ministries and public bodies over the state's secure public network, replacing exchange by CD, key or software interfaces.

DZA.note: Names the national personal data protection authority as the body that will approve data exchanges; its appointment or law not stated.

facts.fact: Algeria's High Commissioner for Digitalisation said the data governance framework meets information security requirements and the laws in force, notably on personal data protection.

The High Commission for Digitalisation says it finalised the first version of a National Data Governance Framework, a regulatory framework for exclusive data exchange between ministries and public bodies that classifies data by sensitivity level and sets encryption and security measures per category.
facts.system: Référentiel national de la gouvernance des données

facts.fact: The High Commissioner for Digitalisation said a national short-term implementation plan (2025-2026) for the National Digital Transformation Strategy, with more than 500 digital projects, was approved in January 2025 by the ministerial departments.
The implementation plan for the National Digital Transformation Strategy comprises more than 500 digital projects for 2025-2026, with no cost stated.
The strategy's short-term national implementation plan runs 2025-2026.
